correctness.rationale: An exact edge-count argument identifies precisely one intact path and one deleted edge on each other path. The leaf polynomial accounts for all endpoint cuts with an explicit terminal correction. For a transfer p,q -> p-1,q+1, direct algebra yields an exact positive convex mixture with auxiliary H. An explicit coupling shows H >= old leaf count for all configurations, with a strictly positive event of strict increase. Elementary majorization transfers give the global extrema. A separate enumerative Python script tested the polynomial against exhaustive small-graph spanning-tree enumeration and 3272 exact assertions; this test is not substituted for the all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The contribution is the explicit generalized-theta leaf generating polynomial plus a strict first-order stochastic comparison for all integer path-length-balancing transfers and its global extremizers. Rapoport gives general finite-graph degree probabilities that may be evaluated on the family, but a generic formula does not state or imply by an immediate parameter substitution the cross-graph stochastic monotonicity; the latter follows from an explicit new convex-mixture identity and a monotone coupling. Noguchi and Zamfirescu determine possible leaf-count supports, not comparative laws. Relevant published record and accessible own claims have been compared semantically; historical priority remains uncertain.
residual_risks: Unindexed or non-English exact leaf enumeration for theta subdivisions may exist; historical priority cannot be certified from searches.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural stochastic optimization problem on the simplest noncactus series-parallel networks, generalized to arbitrarily many internally disjoint paths. Strict stochastic dominance simultaneously controls every increasing leaf-count observable; the mixture coupling provides a structural explanation and global extremizers for fixed total length. The order is not a numerical or single-parameter gain and is not a trivial restatement of a graph-invariant enumeration.
